answers.question: Who are you and what is the baseline?
answers.answer: Two-dentist clinic in a mid-sized UK town. About 35 new patients a month (practice software report), want 60 by June.

answers.question: What do you already have online?
answers.answer: Google Business Profile has 4.6 stars from 140 reviews. Website is WordPress; we can edit it. No ads running now.

answers.question: Rules and limits?
answers.answer: Advertising must follow UK dental and health advertising rules, no before-and-after photos without consent, and no patient data leaves the practice system.

answers.question: What access do we have?

research.approach: Practitioners treat dental growth as a chain: be found locally, turn visits into contact, answer every enquiry quickly, and measure new patients by source. They fix the free, high-intent assets first (an accurate Business Profile with every service listed, mobile pages that make calling or booking one tap) and add paid search only for the treatments worth promoting. In the UK the advertising rules come first, not last: promotional material must be accurate and not misleading, must state NHS or private status and carry GDC details, and before-and-after images must be genuine and representative with signed, dated proof. Tracking is the usual weak spot, because phone calls are the main lead source and are rarely tied to a source, so they count enquiries by channel and judge success by new patients booked, not clicks.

sources.title: ASA and CAP advice: dental advertising
sources.note: Regulator advice. Before-and-after photos must be genuine and representative with signed and dated proof; objective claims need evidence; comparisons need robust evidence.

sources.title: GDC guidance on advertising
sources.note: Effective from 2013-09-30, the latest version the page shows. Accurate and not misleading; state NHS, mixed or private; GDC number on information carrying a name; rules on specialist titles.

sources.title: Google Business Profile guidelines: representing your business
sources.note: Page is undated; date is when it was read (2026-11-02). Name must match the real name, use specific categories, no promotions or prices in the description, one profile per business.

sources.title: How can website visitors be converted into patients? (Dentistry.co.uk)
sources.note: Trade article sponsored by a vendor, so its figures are claims. Several contact options, fast mobile pages, separate journeys for urgent and cosmetic enquiries, measure enquiries divided by visitors.

sources.title: Google Ads Help: Measure calls from ads
sources.note: Page is undated; date is when it was found (2026-11-02). Calls can be counted as conversions by call length or by analysis of recordings; imported call outcomes are the most precise.

sources.title: Conversion tracking setup and repair planner

steps.name: Set the advertising rules and approved claims first
steps.why: UK dental promotion must be accurate, state NHS or private status, carry GDC details and keep proof for every objective claim and every before-and-after image. Agreeing what may be said before anything is written avoids rework and regulator complaints.

steps.name: Find where new patients come from today
steps.why: Growth work starts from the sources of the 35 current new patients: Business Profile actions (calls, directions, website clicks), Search Console queries and the practice software report, kept as counts only.

steps.name: Make enquiries countable by source without patient data
steps.why: Phone calls, forms and online bookings must each be tied to a source, and the practice should count booked first appointments, not clicks. Counts stay in the practice; no names or patient details are shared.

steps.name: Fix the Business Profile and local listings
steps.why: The profile is the main local entry point. Experts check the real name, specific categories, every treatment listed as a service, accurate hours and links, photos with consent, and replies to reviews, and keep promotions out of the description.

steps.name: Make the website easy to book from on a phone
steps.why: Most dental traffic is on phones. Experts give several one-tap ways to contact the practice, fast pages, and separate journeys for urgent and cosmetic visitors, then measure enquiries per visitor.

steps.name: Choose which treatments and searches to go after
steps.why: Search Console shows what people already search for and where the site ranks. The owner still has to say which treatments are worth promoting, since profitability is unknown, before effort or ad money is pointed at them.

steps.name: Test a small, compliant paid search campaign
steps.why: With no ads today, a capped search test on the chosen treatments and the town can show whether paid demand exists. It is started paused, reviewed for advertising rules, and read before the budget grows.

steps.name: Read results against new patients booked
steps.why: The target is new patients, so each month's practice report count is compared with the 35 baseline and with enquiries by source. Search visibility changes take weeks, so single weeks are not judged.

pitfalls.text: Using before-and-after photos without signed, dated consent and proof they are genuine and representative.
Using titles such as specialist or orthodontist that the registrant is not entitled to, or leaving out NHS or private status and GDC details.
Putting prices, offers or promotions in the Business Profile description, or changing the profile name to add keywords.
Counting clicks or enquiries as new patients, or judging search work in a few weeks.
Moving patient details into marketing tools to track results, which breaks the owner's rule.

stages.name: Pin down the goal
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured target, limits, rules and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Agree the advertising rules and approved claims
stages.goal: List the UK dental and health advertising rules that apply, then sort every claim and image already on the website and Business Profile into approved, needs proof or banned. Not legal advice: flag points the practice's indemnity provider or adviser should confirm.

Each existing claim is marked approved, needs proof or banned
Any before-and-after photo is banned unless signed, dated consent and proof it is genuine and representative are on file

stages.name: Gather where new patients come from

stages.name: Find what limits new patients
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses against the evidence and keep competing explanations: visibility, site conversion, enquiry handling, search terms, trust and paid demand. Show which treatments search data supports, and mark treatment profitability as unknown until the owner supplies it.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with its evidence

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked cards, each with the finding behind it, expected effect, effort, confidence, risk, cost and how it will be measured. Include a card for the paid search test only if the evidence supports it, and show treatments that search data supports next to the question of which are worth promoting.

hypotheses.statement: The Business Profile is incomplete or poorly categorised, so too few local searchers find it.
hypotheses.test: Compare categories, services, photos and hours with the local search checklist; look at profile views and actions by month, split into searches for the practice name and other searches if shown.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Services or categories are missing and non-name searches bring few views or actions.
hypotheses.refute_if: The profile is complete and views from non-name searches are healthy and steady.

hypotheses.statement: Visitors reach the website but few call or book.
hypotheses.test: Count clicks needed to call or book on a phone, check mobile speed, and compare contact actions with visits if analytics exist.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Booking takes several steps, pages are slow on a phone, or contact actions per visit are low.
hypotheses.refute_if: Contact is one tap away, pages are fast and contact actions per visit are healthy.

hypotheses.statement: Enquiries arrive but too few become booked first appointments, because of missed calls, slow replies or no free new-patient slots.
hypotheses.test: Four-week tally of enquiries by channel, missed calls, first appointments booked and days to the first free new-patient slot.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A large share of enquiries is not booked, calls are missed, or the first slot is weeks away.
hypotheses.refute_if: Nearly all enquiries are booked quickly.

hypotheses.statement: The site ranks for general or branded terms but not for the treatments that matter.
hypotheses.test: Match Search Console queries and pages to the treatments the owner names; check position and clicks for treatment-plus-town searches.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Treatment searches have impressions but low position or no treatment page ranks.
hypotheses.refute_if: Treatment pages already rank well and take clicks.

hypotheses.statement: Nearby practices look more trustworthy because they have more or newer reviews, or reply more often.
hypotheses.test: Compare review count, recency and reply rate with three nearby practices' public profiles.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Competitors have clearly more recent reviews or reply to most reviews while this practice does not.
hypotheses.refute_if: The practice matches or beats nearby practices.

hypotheses.statement: People search for the chosen treatments in the town and no paid result from this practice captures them.
hypotheses.test: Check search volume and who shows for the chosen treatment-plus-town searches; judge by a small capped paid test, not by estimates.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Searches exist and a capped test produces enquiries that become booked first appointments at a cost the owner accepts.
hypotheses.refute_if: Searches are few, or the test brings clicks and calls that do not book.

measurement.window: Monthly, for at least three months after the first approved change; search visibility changes take weeks.
measurement.min_volume: Judge on monthly new-patient counts from the practice report; read the ad test only after the owner and AI agree, before launch, the number of enquiries needed.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause any ad at once if a rules check fails or spend reaches the monthly cap; otherwise read results after the full window.
